extracted.subtask_description: Daily newspaper reporting of wartime events, government actions, policy recommendations, and legal rulings for a general audience; includes datelined Associated Press dispatches and government announcements.

rubrics_metrics.name: High command urged (Senate war mobilization committee)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Senate war mobilization committee called for a domestic 'high command' to make sure that the nation's energies shall 'no longer be dissipated by loose management.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The committee cited a lack of centralized direction and failure to mobilize fully the will and energies of all groups and recommended establishment of a central domestic 'high command' to coordinate mobilization as troops gird for great offensive actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Across-the-board price control
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation: Across-the-board price control 'at all levels of production and distribution.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed by the Senate war mobilization committee as one of the measures the proposed 'high command' should implement to prevent dissipated energies on the home front.

rubrics_metrics.name: Production and allocation to support rationing
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation: Production and allocation of basic food and clothing supplies to support rationing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee recommended central direction of production and allocation to ensure rationing needs are met on the home front.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single policy on subsidies
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation: The formation and execution of a single policy on subsidies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the committee's suggested measures to centralize economic controls and eliminate conflicting subsidy policies during wartime mobilization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish requirements committee
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation: Establishment of a requirements committee to inquire into military, lend-lease and civilian needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee proposed a body to assess and coordinate requirements across military, allied (lend-lease) and civilian demands to better allocate scarce resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participation of management, labor and agriculture in mobilization board
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation: Participation by management, labor and agriculture in a war mobilization board working under direction of the Office of War Mobilization (OWM).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee envisaged inclusive representation to align production, labor, and agricultural policy under centralized mobilization direction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incentive wage plans to spur war production
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation: Implementation of incentive wage plans to spur war production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed by the committee as a measure to increase productivity and output on the home front.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporary anthracite distribution program (community limits and committees)
rubrics_metrics.description: Temporary program limiting each community to the amount of hard (anthracite) coal delivered during a base period (April–August 1942) or five-twelfths of the coal shipped from April 1942 to March 1943, whichever is larger; establishment of a national and six regional anthracite distribution committees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program effective tomorrow (from report date). Aimed to insure every community its fair share of anthracite; regions enumerated and anthracite sizes affected were 'egg, stove, chestnut and pea.' Committees to be set up to administer distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freeze on railroad-borne bituminous coal in transit
rubrics_metrics.description: Secretary Ickes 'froze' an estimated 3,000,000 tons of railroad-borne bituminous coal in transit as a means of making fuel available to war industries and other essential users.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users having less than ten days' supply of bituminous coal may apply to their railroad for delivery; measure restores earlier War Production Board directive and was intended to prioritize war-essential uses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Civil Aeronautics Board postwar airline application relaxation
rubrics_metrics.description: Civil Aeronautics Board relaxed wartime regulation to permit consideration of applications for authority to establish new domestic airline services after the war (applications had been held in abeyance since Dec. 12, 1941).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Change intended to expedite post-war expansion and enable airlines to speed conversion of their equipment and personnel from war to peacetime operations; foreign-route applications remained excluded from this relaxation.

rubrics_metrics.name: War Shipping Administration 'upgrading' training standards
rubrics_metrics.description: War Shipping Administration to establish upgrading schools to provide skilled manpower for the merchant marine: third mates and third assistant engineers may take a course of about thirty days to become second mates/assistant engineers; ordinary seamen may become able-bodied seamen in less than fifteen days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: to supply skilled manpower for the expanding merchant marine; schools to be established in New York, New Orleans and San Francisco ports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supreme Court denaturalization evidentiary standard (Schneiderman decision)
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal standard: A naturalized alien's citizenship cannot be canceled simply because he belonged to the Communist party; denaturalization requires 'clear, unequivocal and convincing evidence' that he obtained citizenship illegally (e.g., was not attached to the Constitution or advocated present violent action).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court emphasized the distinction between theoretical/doctrinal advocacy and present violent action that creates a 'clear and present danger'; where two reasonable interpretations of an organization's program exist, denaturalization is not justified absent convincing proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Military commander authority for curfew in endangered sections
rubrics_metrics.description: Supreme Court upheld that a military commander may adopt a curfew on persons of Japanese ancestry on the West Coast (exercise of war powers) when deemed necessary to guard against sabotage and espionage in endangered sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opinion noted such measures go 'to the brink of constitutional power' and were upheld on narrow grounds; court majority accepted military necessity but cautioned about constitutional limits.
